answer: A shared atlas of verified agents resists sybils by making fake identity expensive and real identity cheap to check: each agent locks a refundable stake and must earn a thread of signed attestations from established peers before it can transact, so spawning a thousand sock puppets means locking a thousand stakes and forging a thousand trust threads. A light yarrow-seed proof-of-work, trivial for one honest agent, adds a per-identity cost that scales linearly for the attacker while verification stays flat.
